title: Ops cadence & delivery brief: stability, hires, and Q3 priorities
customer_attendees: Several remote offices: SF, London, Dublin, Bangalore
summary: Quick mid-year operational check: stability incidents, hiring cadence, delivery timelines for Q3 features, a short demo of the new cost dashboard, and Q&A. Leadership aligned on two hires and a hiring freeze exception flow; reliability team to run a 48-hour soak and report back. Packed with clarifying questions about Dedicated capacity SLAs and private deployment timelines.
next_steps: Marcus to run 48-hour soak and share findings by 2026-07-10
Priya to finalize hiring plan and share hiring tracker by 2026-07-15
Samir to circulate the Q3 delivery risk register and owners by 2026-07-12
Product to publish short notes on Dedicated SLA expectations and fallbacks by 2026-07-13
Lina to open two urgent reqs and start screening the week of 2026-07-13
action_items: Marcus Li - run 48-hour soak for inference runtime and report - 2026-07-10
Priya Nair - finalize hiring cadence and headcount exceptions doc - 2026-07-15
Samir Patel - share Q3 delivery risk register and mitigation owners - 2026-07-12
Lina Gomez - open two urgent senior infra roles and begin outreach - 2026-07-13
Daniel Cho - validate Dedicated capacity regression tests with infra by 2026-07-14
questions: How are we tracking against latency SLOs after last week's kernel roll?
Can we fast-track two infra hires without breaking the current hiring guardrails?
Where's the risk on Private deployments for the enterprise pilot in September?
What's the plan for cost-awareness controls for customers using streaming endpoints?
transcript:
[00:00] Eve Martin: Good morning everyone, thanks for joining. We'll try to keep this tight, 55 minutes. Quick agenda: reliability update, hiring cadence, Q3 delivery, quick cost-dashboard peek, then Q&A.
[00:12] Daniel Cho: Hi all, I'll start with reliability. We saw a series of short tail latency spikes on Tuesday after the kernel update, roughly 2 to 8 p99 blips across a subset of Dedicated hosts. Marcus led initial triage.
[00:25] Marcus Li: Yeah, the spikes correlated with a specific quantization path on a 4-bit variant, uh, and the issue mainly affected sequences above 2k tokens. We mitigated by rolling back that kernel on the affected pool and routing requests to the fallback variant.
[00:40] Priya Nair: Just to confirm, rollback impacted throughput at peak for about 30 minutes, right? We should quantify cost delta.
[00:48] Marcus Li: Correct, about 12% throughput loss for the small window; cost delta is still being computed. We'll include exact numbers in today's follow-up.
[00:56] Samir Patel: This is the second time we've had a perf regression after a kernel tweak in the last four months. Can we get a more formal pre-prod soak, maybe 48-hour for major kernel changes?
[01:08] Daniel Cho: Agreed. We're planning to add a mandatory soak for anything touching the execution path. Marcus will run a 48-hour soak this week on the staging pool that mirrors Dedicated configurations.
[01:21] Marcus Li: Yep, I'll kick that off today. Also, small note: telemetry missed one rollout flag due to a tagging bug, so some hosts weren't flagged as part of the rollout. We'll patch the rollout tool.
[01:33] Eve Martin: Ok, good. Hiring — Priya?
[01:36] Priya Nair: Hard to summarize: hiring is slow in infra, we have a bottleneck in senior infra engineers and SREs. Lina's team is prioritizing two urgent reqs. We have an internal headcount freeze for non-critical roles this quarter, but we need exceptions.
[01:48] Lina Gomez: We're proposing two exceptions: a senior infra engineer and a senior reliability engineer. We have strong referrals in the pipeline, could accelerate interviews.
[01:56] Priya Nair: My ask is to approve those two exceptions and keep the rest on hold. We'll provide a hiring cadence doc with milestones and scorecards.
[02:05] Eve Martin: I support the exceptions for infra. Marcus, Priya, you're owners to make the case and present the hiring scorecard by next week.
[02:12] Priya Nair: Will do.
[02:14] Samir Patel: On Q3 delivery: main commitments are the cost dashboard GA, Dedicated autoscaling improvements, and Private deployment pilot for the regulated customer. There are a couple of cross-team dependencies with platform and sales engineering.
[02:28] Daniel Cho: For Dedicated autoscaling, we still need to validate burst capacity policies under sustained load; our internal perf tests simulate synthetic traffic but not KV-cache heavy workloads.
[02:38] Marcus Li: Right, we'll add KV-cache-heavy scenarios to the soak and run a long-tailed request distribution. That's part of the 48-hour soak scope.
[02:45] Eve Martin: Samir, what's the realistic ship window for cost dashboard GA?
[02:48] Samir Patel: If we stay on plan and no major regressions, late August for a soft GA. But we have a couple of outstanding UX items and a final privacy review.
[02:58] Audience: (murmurs)
[03:01] Eve Martin: Let's do a quick demo of the dashboard — Samir, over to you.
[03:04] Samir Patel: I'll share my screen — (audio: minor pause) — ok. The cost dashboard surfaces token-level cost, per-model breakdowns, per-route latency histograms, and an alerts panel for anomalous spend. There's also a predictive cost model that estimates monthly spend given current patterns.
[03:23] Samir Patel: Note: the predictive model currently underestimates burst costs for streaming endpoints; this is a known bias. We'll adjust the model once we ingest more streaming telemetry.
[03:35] Priya Nair: Could we add an option to pin a model-version baseline so teams can compare cost after a quantization or kernel change?
[03:42] Samir Patel: Yes, that's on the roadmap — model baselines and regression diffs.
[03:46] Audience: (applause, some chuckles)
[03:50] Daniel Cho: Quick note on Private deployments: Sales has a pilot slated for Sept onboarding with a regulated customer in EU. Network team is still validating the VPC peering flows and KMS integrations. We need to harden the onboarding checklist by mid-July or we risk slipping.
[04:06] Eve Martin: Who owns the checklist?
[04:08] Daniel Cho: Platform + Security. Marcus will coordinate with Sarah in Security.
[04:12] Marcus Li: I'll sync with Sarah after this call.
[04:15] Eve Martin: Questions from the floor?
[04:18] Employee 1: Are we changing our stance on Dedicated SLAs for the mid-market tier? We have a request from a customer to bump latency SLOs.
[04:26] Samir Patel: We can do a tiered approach: higher SLA for reserved capacity customers with a price delta, but we need to quantify cost and failure modes.
[04:35] Employee 2: On the hiring freeze exception — what's the approval process?
[04:38] Lina Gomez: Submit a formal request in the hiring tracker, include scorecard, urgency rationale, and approvals from Eng VP and CFO. We'll fast-track reviews for infra exceptions.
[04:49] Eve Martin: Good. A few quick updates from teams — Reliability first: Marcus?
[04:54] Marcus Li: Aside from the soak, we're adding an alert to detect rollout-tagging anomalies and an automated rollback rule if p99 spikes > 200ms for more than two intervals. Also working on a canary dataset that better matches customer distributions.
[05:08] Priya Nair: For platform: we'll pause non-essential feature branches starting next Monday to focus on the soak and Dedicated autoscaling work. That should reduce context switching.
[05:19] Daniel Cho: For infra: kernel selection logic is being extended to consider sequence length histograms; that's scheduled for review next Tuesday.
[05:28] Eve Martin: Let's surface blockers: anything stopping the Private deployment pilot?
[05:32] Security Lead (remote): We have an open item on HSM integration testing with vendor X; test harness is ready, need vendor access.
[05:40] Samir Patel: Sales says the customer is flexible on timeline but prefers September. We should aim to have a dry-run in August.
[05:47] Eve Martin: Ok. Final Q&A — cost controls?
[05:50] Finance Rep: We want a knob to enforce soft quotas on streaming endpoints to avoid runaway costs.
[05:55] Samir Patel: There's an opt-in limit today, we'll formalize an enforcement policy and add an alerting flow.
[06:02] Employee 3: Any update on open source benchmarks for our runtime vs competitor XYZ?
[06:09] Daniel Cho: We're prepping a reproducible benchmark that includes KV-cache and batching behavior; target to publish in August. It'll include a clear methodology appendix.
[06:18] Eve Martin: Great. Quick recap of next steps: Marcus 48-hour soak; Priya hiring plan; Samir risk register; Lina open reqs; Daniel finalize Dedicated tests. We'll close with gratitude — thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.
[06:35] (End of recording)

Notes on transcript: speaker labels are inferred; occasional mis-attributions and transcription artifacts present. References: hiring tracker (internal link), Dedicated-SLA-deck (internal), cost-dashboard-demo (recording link).
